name: Montana

fees.note: Overweight trip permit: $3.50 per 5,000 lb of EXCESS AXLE weight per 25-mile increment (= $0.056 per excess ton-mile). MDT rounds weight up to the next 5,000 lb and miles up to the next 25 mi, and excess is summed per axle group, not gross minus 80,000 - treat as an estimate. Loads over the bridge formula but with legal axle weights instead pay $10 (<=100 mi), $30 (101-199 mi) or $50 (200+ mi).

restrictions.text: Interstate: travel allowed 24/7 up to 18' wide (lights full length and width), including holidays/holiday weekends; loads over 18' wide cannot travel on holidays or holiday weekends.

Non-interstate: 24/7 up to 10' wide, 150' long, 15'6" high; larger loads daylight only. Holidays/holiday weekends: over 10' to 12'6" wide daylight only; over 12'6" wide, 150' long or 15'6" high no travel.

Holidays: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Fourth of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas. Holiday on Fri/Sat bans Fri-Sun; on Sun/Mon bans Sat-Mon; on Tue-Thu bans that day; Thanksgiving bans Thu-Sun (ARM 18.8.101).
Non-interstate: over 18' wide - no weekend travel.
Non-interstate: over 150' long - no weekend travel.
Non-interstate: over 17' high - no weekend travel.

Overweight bridge conditions printed on the permit: max 55 mph, one overweight vehicle per bridge, no stopping/shifting on bridges; non-interstate 10 mph on bridges; centerline-crossing condition needs daylight travel and one front + one rear pilot on non-interstate routes.
No travel when MDT places a route under severe driving conditions. Pilot-escorted moves must not delay traffic more than 15 minutes.

notes: No police-escort or mandatory route-survey thresholds were found in MDT's published permit documents; permittee is responsible for checking clearances. Superloads go through eTRIPs district approval (class 1 decision within 2 working days, class 2 within 5).
Overweight bridge conditions may add pilot vehicles on non-interstate routes (1 rear for the 10-mph condition, 1 front + 1 rear for centerline crossing) - assigned per permit, not modeled as escorts.

Legal gross depends on the bridge formula and axle count (single 20,000, tandem 34,000; up to 131,060 lb for long combinations). Calculator uses 80,000 lb for a 5-axle combination; for longer/heavier configurations the actual excess (and fee) may be lower.
Montana counts a load as oversize over 8'6" wide, 14' high, 75' overall (with overhang), single unit over 55', or trailer over 53'.
